mbm-0318.clue: My practice green has a trapdoor.
mbm-0318.quote: I roll putts across the hall carpet into the empty heating vent. My sister catches the ball downstairs. Yesterday she started charging a biscuit for every return.

mbm-0319.clue: The orange square smells like cedar.
mbm-0319.quote: I cut it from the little bag my grandmother used to keep in her dresser. I filled the quilt square with fresh cedar shavings. The quilt smells like opening her top drawer.

mbm-0320.clue: Our practice sword used to hold up a curtain.
mbm-0320.quote: We wrapped the old wooden curtain rod in soft cloth for slow partner drills. It still has a brass ring at one end. If the stroke wobbles, the ring politely tells on me.

mbm-0321.clue: I left the bootprints in the plaster.
mbm-0321.quote: I pressed my model robot into wet scenery and tried to lift it straight out. It slipped sideways. Now my whole display is the story of a giant robot losing its footing on an icy Tuesday.

mbm-0322.clue: There’s a star in my ticket book.
mbm-0322.quote: The projectionist stamped a star beside the first film I saw on my own. When my younger cousin went solo, I lent him my old ticket for company. He brought back two stars.

mbm-0323.clue: I draw the last position on a napkin.
mbm-0323.quote: Our chess table is next to the snack stand. When it starts raining I draw where the pieces were, fold the napkin and run. We’ve finished some of our best games over two separate lunches.

mbm-0324.quote: My sister and I made up a rule for our garden video game. We each pick a real snail on the glass tank and whoever gets to the lettuce first chooses the next level. It’s a leisurely tournament.

mbm-0325.clue: The photographer only caught one glove.
mbm-0325.quote: I wore white gloves to our dance night so my friend could spot me. In the club photo you can see one white hand above the crowd. My friend had borrowed the other one and was waving right back.

mbm-0326.clue: I can sing that note through a paper tube.
mbm-0326.quote: My cousin made a megaphone from the middle of a wrapping-paper roll. The first time I sang into it our dog came to inspect the far end for a second singer.

mbm-0327.clue: I brought the route home on my hand.
mbm-0327.quote: I sketched the climbing route on the back of my hand while my partner tried it. The last hold was right at the base of my thumb. I could see the whole route when we high-fived.

mbm-0328.clue: There’s a zipper under the sun.
mbm-0328.quote: I made my mum a beach quilt with a little sun in the corner. Unzip it and there’s a dry pocket for her bus fare. She counts the coins without getting a grain of sand in the seams.

mbm-0329.clue: The leather is dark where the thumb goes.
mbm-0329.quote: I made a handle cover for my father’s old lunch pail. I thought the first worn spot would spoil it. When he brought it back for oiling, it was the exact shape of his hand.

mbm-0330.clue: The record is one fridge magnet wide.
mbm-0330.quote: We track our lifting sessions on the garage refrigerator. I move a tiny yellow magnet one square each time I finish a set. When it reaches the handle my brother opens the lemonade.

mbm-0331.clue: I didn’t keep the big antenna.
mbm-0331.quote: Our smallest antenna picked up a station my fancy one kept missing. It’s clipped to a bamboo ruler now. The ruler used to measure my homework margins and is enjoying a much bigger assignment.

mbm-0332.clue: You can hear the spoon before the birds.
mbm-0332.quote: My camping buddy taps a spoon inside a mug to wake me when the coffee is ready. Once a woodpecker tapped back. We set out a third mug to be polite.

mbm-0333.clue: I know the turn by its smell.
mbm-0333.quote: Our ballroom class meets in the bakery after closing. On the last turn by the window you catch the smell of cinnamon bread. My partner says I always find the right step over there.

mbm-0334.clue: I carry one glass marble in the canoe.
mbm-0334.quote: I put it on the middle seat when we pack for a trip. If the boat leans the marble rolls straight to whoever brought too many books. I’m usually the one repacking.

mbm-0335.clue: My lucky lift ticket has a tea ring.
mbm-0335.quote: I folded an old ticket under the wobbly café table where my dad and I stop between runs. We left it there at closing. Next season it was still holding the table steady.

mbm-0336.clue: The plain handprint is the one I visit.
mbm-0336.quote: At the tile museum there’s a brick with a maker’s palm pressed into the back. Every time I see it I spread my fingers in the air. Somebody my size turned that brick over years ago.

mbm-0337.clue: The umbrella drew the best crowd.
mbm-0337.quote: I bought an umbrella painted with a huge fried egg. The first rainy day at the market three people asked where to find the café. I led them to the stall that makes breakfast.

mbm-0338.clue: The white stripes disappear at noon.
mbm-0338.quote: On the morning ski run I can see every ridge from the grooming machine. At lunch the sun smooths the whole hill with light. I like skiing the same path twice and finding two slopes.

mbm-0339.clue: The scarf goes round the whole circle.
mbm-0339.quote: Someone brought a long blue scarf to the village folk dance. We passed it hand to hand during the slow part. When the tune sped up it lifted right off our wrists like a wave.

mbm-0340.clue: Our replay board is made of biscuits.
mbm-0340.quote: We ran out of daylight before we could clear up the baduk game. At breakfast my nephew copied the last corner with pale and dark biscuits. He ate my best move before I could defend it.

mbm-0341.clue: The scoreboard thinks my mum is asleep.
mbm-0341.quote: She tried my puzzle game while I made tea and beat my high score. She held one button too long and picked the same sleepy face three times. For six months our champion has appeared to be asleep.

mbm-0342.clue: I’ve only been paid in pears.
mbm-0342.quote: I sang beside a fruit stall while they repaired the sound system at our fair. The owner dropped a ripe pear in my hat after every song. I went home hoarse and made a very good crumble.
